## Claims

### C-R0-01 — Hubbard: NICOT evangelical balance
**Locus:** L169–L179 (General Editor’s Preface, Robert L. Hubbard Jr.)  
**Quote/anchor:** “NICOT delicately balances ‘criticism’ (i.e., the use of standard critical methodologies) with humble respect… for the biblical text.”  
**Claim:** Hubbard presents NICOT as evangelical: Bible as God’s inspired Word; not mere ancient artifact; aims for scholars, clergy, and serious students; lineage Young → Harrison → Hubbard.

### C-R0-02 — Longman: fifteen years; Akkadian dissertation hook
**Locus:** L185  
**Quote/anchor:** “The book of Ecclesiastes has captured my attention… for the past fifteen years… Mesopotamian literary texts that formed the substance of my doctoral dissertation at Yale… formal, structural similarity to the body of the book of Ecclesiastes.”  
**Claim:** Academic entry point is ANE/Mesopotamian autobiographical genre (Yale dissertation); formal parallel to Ecclesiastes body is the planned intro argument.

### C-R0-03 — Qohelet’s question modern; answers shocking in canon
**Locus:** L187–L189  
**Quote/anchor:** “Where can we find meaning in the world?” / “‘Meaningless,’ says Qohelet, ‘everything is meaningless.’ How does this perspective fit into the rest of biblical revelation?”  
**Claim:** Longman frames the commentary’s driving question as reconciling Qohelet’s *hebel* verdict with canonical revelation; Qohelet named as main speaker.

### C-R0-04 — Dedication to Dan Allender; psychology + OT
**Locus:** L205  
**Quote/anchor:** “This book is dedicated to Dan Allender… Dan’s insight into the human condition and the Bible has stimulated much of my thinking about the book of Ecclesiastes.”  
**Claim:** Pastoral-psychological partnership with Allender shapes Longman’s reading of human despair/meaning-seeking in Ecclesiastes.

### C-R0-05 — Institutional setting and series history
**Locus:** L193–L201  
**Quote/anchor:** Harrison invitation; Hubbard editing; Westminster OT colleagues (Dillard, Waltke, Groves, Green, Enns); doctoral seminar on Ecclesiastes.  
**Claim:** Commentary produced over long period at Westminster with seminar testing of ideas; Waltke named as former colleague (relevant for Proverbs/Ecclesiastes tension in wiki).

## Coverage report
